slot.brief: Arrange given carbanions/radicals by stability with a stated reason (resonance, inductive effects).

stem: Considering resonance and electron-withdrawing effects, arrange these carbanions in decreasing order of stability: I. $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2^-$, II. $\text{N}\equiv\text{CCH}_2^-$, III. $\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCH}_2^-$, IV. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2^-$.

verdicts.working: The carbonyl-stabilized anion (I) is more stable than the cyano-stabilized anion (II); allylic resonance stabilizes III more than the unstabilized ethyl carbanion IV. Thus I > II > III > IV.

working:
$\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2^-$: charge delocalized onto O; $\text{N}\equiv\text{CCH}_2^-$: delocalized onto N.
Allyl anion: charge delocalized over two C atoms; ethyl anion: no resonance stabilization.
Conjugate-acid $pK_a$ values are approximately $19$, $25$, $43$, and $50$, respectively.
Lower conjugate-acid $pK_a$ implies a more stable conjugate base: $\text{I} > \text{II} > \text{III} > \text{IV}$.
